spec: WALK_BESIDE v0.1 (design repo, private): the Keepers' first word, the cut shown on screen, the hold lines and the walk-beside mechanic. Decisions D1960-D1979.
_about: Ours, not a design copy. Act 1: the Weir Hut lantern's story.chi_done line (objPatch, ahead of the built else) and two one-step runs chained after their settled ACT1_KEEPER_JOIN scenes (sceneTails on chi_report and night_watch). Acts 2-5, the Summit and the endings: every scene is built behind its real flags, so it stays inert in normal play until its beat is built: wb_charter chains after cab_pt1 (a sceneTail that waits for that scene), wb_cut plays at the Hearthmoor Lodge steps on story.cab_seat, Ilse's stayer letter comes through a Lantern House Host (hostNotes), wb_pres chains after pres_cabinet_last. Scenes whose host scene or map is not built yet (the springs stop on Kilnmouth, Quinn's N2k2, the Ledger Night's L13a, the Spire rows, the Summit lines) are here as scenes for that build to run, and `waits` lists each hook. Save stays pixelpets.save.v2, v 2: every flag here is an additive story.* key (NOT_STEPS), nothing is written at load. Every line is PLACEHOLDER until Story signs it (D1960-D1979).

_placeholders.note: PLACEHOLDER copy (Story to sign): every player line in this file. The speaker key 'Vincent Chi' is the raw cast key; it shows as Jacob Chi (NAMES_PASS D1730, display only). hostNotes[0].line is Story's (STORY_LINES D2143).

objPatch._note: WALK_BESIDE §4.1 (D1970): one new key on the Weir Hut's old Keeper lantern, ahead of the built else (unchanged). §3.3: Mo's repeat on hq_mo, after every story key and before standing.keepers>=1. §2.1 (D1963): the charter case's three keyed tap lines, for the CABINET build's T3 prop in hc_gov_2 (id hc_gov_charter); inert until that object exists.

linesFirst.story.chi_done: The cloth is off the old lantern. Scratched on the base: WHERE THEY STOP, STOP.

add.story.wb_cut & !story.side=glimmer: Both lines are still in the tin.

linesFirst.story.wb_cut: Both lines, under glass. Every notice in the country prints the first.
linesFirst.story.wb_springs: THE FIRST WORD. Where they stop, stop. {pet} did, on the Kilnmouth hill path.
linesFirst.else: THE FIRST WORD. Walk beside them, not ahead. Where they stop, stop. Where they turn, look.

addObjs.name: Archivist Mo
addObjs._note: WALK_BESIDE §3.3 (D1961): Mo by the Lodge steps with the tin box, Act 2 (story.cab_seat) until the cut is shown. The Lodge door is at 15,6 on today's Hearthmoor (detail_wayup), so the packet's 12,7 / 11,7 move one door east: Mo at 14,7, the trigger on 15,7.

WALK_BESIDE §3.3: the tile in front of the Lodge door (15,6). With Mo on 14,7, the sign on 16,7 and the fence on 17,6, every walk to the door lands here first, so no holder reaches B9 without the cut.

sceneTails._note: WALK_BESIDE §4.1 (D1970): each a one-step run after its settled scene; chi_report ends once chi_hub returns (That's all sets story.chi_done), and the guard keeps an interrupted report from playing it early. §2.2 (D1963) and §4.5 (D1967): wb_charter after cab_pt1 and wb_pres after pres_cabinet_last; a tail on a scene that is not built yet is skipped, so both wait inert for CABINET S1 and PRESIDENT_SCENES K2b.

hostNotes._note: WALK_BESIDE §4.3 (D1965): the stayer's letter from Ilse through the first Lantern House Host after Rook's offer and R5. A letter, not a report: nothing to send back. Never for a switcher or the loyalist.
hostNotes.line: A letter for you, sealed with the Warden's lantern. No reply wanted, this time.

wb_chi_lantern: Jacob Chi lifts the cloth off the old lantern on the shelf.
Scouts learned the long version once. Nobody asks for it now.
wb_scout_watch: Walk beside, not ahead. Tonight that meant I stood here and wrote it down.
wb_charter: As the room empties, the Governor stops you at a glass case by the stair.
Under the glass, an old page with a wax seal like a feather: WALK BESIDE THEM, NOT AHEAD.
Below it, a second line: WHERE THEY STOP, STOP. WHERE THEY TURN, LOOK.
Lovely, isn't it? We print the first line. It fits on a notice.
Before my time. Your Keepers keep older paper than I do. Ask at home.
Doesn't it? Brass and glass, and still the best line in the building.
wb_cut: Archivist Mo is waiting by the Lodge steps with a flat tin box.
The Governor's office wired: a Cadet asked about the glass. I have the answer.
Cadet. You sit at the Governor's table now. Then you should see what it signed.
A yellowed notice proof: WALK BESIDE THEM, NOT AHEAD. WHERE THEY STOP, STOP. WHERE THEY TURN, LOOK.
The second line is struck through in red. In the margin: FIRST LINE ONLY. FOR THE DURATION.
Stamped below: THE WAR CABINET, HIGH CHARITY, FOR THE PRESIDENT. A Great War date.
In the war, Walklings kept turning for home. Holders looked, as the word said. Then they followed.
So the table kept the half that keeps you together. It cut the half that lets them lead.
Commanders get both lines with their rank. Old Scouts kept it by mouth. The rest of us get the notice.
Back in the tin, then. The war ended. Nobody ever lifted the order.
I write it down. I do not say what it means.
In the company's back room they asked Walklings to listen too. They meant something else.
The whole word is on your STANDING card.
wb_springs: {pet} stops at the foot of the hill path and won't go on.
You stop with it. Up the hill the cloud sits flat, and nothing moves.
wb_quinn_n2k2: Your Keepers cut their own word in half. We kept the half that says look.
wb_ilse_letter: A letter from Warden Ilse, in her small, exact hand.
Word travels along the lanterns. They say the company offered you a desk.
Steering is walking ahead with a lamp. I'd sooner walk beside in the dark.
wb_ledger_l13a: Feed, rest, listen. I listened so well they could follow my counts.
wb_pres: On his way out, the President stops at the glass case by the stair.
Walk beside them, by all means. Somebody still walks ahead of the country.
wb_spire: The company kept my last words and dropped the first. {pet} kept all of it.
Your Keepers kept my first words and lost the rest. {pet} kept all of it.
wb_summit: Walk beside them. It was the only thing I ever asked of you.
{pet} turns late, the way it does now. You are beside it to see.
{pet} comes to stand beside you. Where it looks, you look.

endCards._note: WALK_BESIDE §4.8 (D1969): one notice card per ending, after the town cards and before the Rook line. The epilogue screen (REPORTS_AND_ENDINGS) is not built: this is its data.
endCards.k_restored: New Keeper notices go up in every town, both lines, in the old type.
endCards.k_court: The Court lifts a war order nobody remembered. The notices get their second line back.
endCards.k_desk: The notices stay as they were. The first line still fits the board.
endCards.l_hand: His office reprints the notices: the first line only, in bigger type.
endCards.l_witness: The war order turns up in his files. The Court puts the second line back.
endCards.g_turned: On the Lodge board one Keeper notice stays up. Someone has pencilled in the second line.
endCards.g_order: The Keepers' notices come down. The company's go up, one word each: LISTEN.
endCards.g_road: You walk the Climb at {pet}'s pace. Where it stops, you stop.
